tasks.notes: Multi-path retry overwrites the retried-wave evidence. `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` allows one retry *per path* per attempt (`retriedPaths` is a Set, and the loop re-enters for each newly-red path), but the kept copy is always the single directory `evidenceWaveDirOf(attemptKey + '-retried')`, and the retry block opens with `fs.rmSync(kept, { recursive: true, force: true })`. If a second, different joined path goes red after the first retry, the first retried wave — the only surviving record of that path's first resolver reply, since its run-tree wave was removed — is deleted. The CONTRACT sentence this task adds reads the same way (`frontier/wave-<attempt>-retried/` … `the wave a red check re-folded, kept whole`, singular). M2 and legs (b)/(e) only exercise a single retry, so nothing in the exam catches it. Suggested fix: name the kept directory per retry (e.g. `wave-<attempt>-retried-<k>` with k = checkRetries+1, or `wave-<attempt>-retried-<path-slug>`), and widen the CONTRACT literal accordingly — note that changing the literal would also need leg (h)'s `wave-<attempt>-retried` grep to still match.; `resolversDispatched` silently drops a dispatch that produced no reply. The new `agent` wrapper in `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` does `const reply = await dispatch(text, agentOpts); if (reply) resolversDispatched += 1`, replacing BASE's `resolversDispatched = resolution.transcripts.length`. Switching to a per-dispatch counter is required by the task's Context ("counts REAL dispatches only", 2 on a retried single-conflict fold), but the `if (reply)` guard goes further than that: a dispatch that returns null/undefined, or one whose call throws (caught inside `resolveConflicts`), still cost a model invocation and would have been a transcript at BASE, yet now increments nothing. `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` branches on `resolversDispatched` being non-zero when it decides whether the PR body gets a resolver section, so an all-null resolver round would now render as a resolver-less fold. `resolversDispatched += 1` unconditionally (before the `return reply`) matches both BASE's meaning and the Context's.; unverified: the stated acceptance is `suite — the committed suite is the verification`, but the executed evidence covers only this task's own exam (`node fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs`), the two Proof `Run:` commands and the one constraint `Check:`. This diff adds `checks`/`checkRetries` to every `publish-fold/receipt.json` attempt row and to every `driver:publish-fold` event, and changes what `resolversDispatched` counts — fields that `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs` and `fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` read. Those sims plant their own receipts rather than calling `publishFold`, so the risk is low, but nothing in the evidence settles it. Running the full committed suite (or at least `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs`) on this tree would settle it.; Evidence-name collision when two different joined paths each earn a retry in one attempt. `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` allows one retry per path (`retriedPaths` is keyed by path, and the `for(;;)` loop re-enters the retry branch for a second, different red path), but the kept-wave name is fixed at `evidenceWaveDirOf(attemptKey + '-retried')`. The second retry's `fs.rmSync(kept, …)` + `fs.cpSync(waveDirOf(attemptKey), kept, …)` overwrites the first retried wave, so `frontier/wave-<attempt>-retried/` ends up holding only the last discarded wave and the earlier pass's replies are gone from the evidence tree. The exam never reaches this shape (legs (b), (e), (f) each retry exactly one path), and the fix cannot be made inside this task alone: `frontier/wave-<attempt>-retried/` is the literal M4 pins in `fleet/CONTRACT.md` and the Proof's second `Run:` greps for it, so a per-retry suffix would have to be settled in the plan's text as well as in `fleet/publish-fold.mjs`.; `replayReply` in `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` degrades silently to a live dispatch. It returns `null` on three distinct failures — no conflicts-index entry for the path in the retried wave, `fs.readdirSync(r.waveDir)` throwing, or no `reply-<i>-<n>` directory matching — and the caller (`agent`) treats `null` as "not replayable" and falls straight through to `dispatch(text, agentOpts)`. That converts a corrupt or missing saved reply into an extra model dispatch for a conflict the Context says must be answered "without dispatching", with nothing in the receipt or the event log distinguishing it from a real first-pass dispatch. The dispatch is lawful (same resolver role, same `RESOLVER_SCHEMA`), so nothing in the exam catches it. Worth either a comment stating the fallback is deliberate, or an `eventLog.onEvent` note when a replay was expected and could not be read.; `resolversDispatched` now under-counts a dispatch that yields no reply. The new wrapper in `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` does `const reply = await dispatch(text, agentOpts); if (reply) resolversDispatched += 1`, where BASE set `resolversDispatched = resolution.transcripts.length` — which counted a transcript whose dispatch returned nothing. The Context redefines the field as "REAL dispatches" and a dispatch that returned a falsy reply was still real, so a fold whose resolver answers with nothing records one fewer than it spent. No leg exercises a falsy reply (`stubAgent` always returns an object, `noAgent()` throws), so the exam does not distinguish the two; `if (reply !== undefined)` or an unconditional increment would match the stated meaning.; concern: scope-judgment: the Context's dispositions-sentence clause names two check reasons — `cannot fold` with `<path> does not parse` and, parenthesized "(for Task 2 to fill)", `suite red` with `<exam> red on <path>`. I wrote only the first. M4 pins only `does not parse`, the Proof's grep `Run:` checks only the four literals I added, and the global constraint says no document may name a mechanism that is not there — the `<exam> red on <path>` mechanism lands with Task 2, so its sentence text is left for Task 2 to add.; concern: behaviour-change: the integration clone is now borrowed, fetched and laid on the candidate's tree even when `args.json` carries no `testCmd`, because the checks must run there regardless. Leg (c.3)'s BASE assertions (no `bash` call, no `suite-1.txt`, `suite: 'none'`) still hold — only extra git calls in the clone are added.

unverified: the Claim's outer sentence — "the resolver brief carries the frontier sibling's task body, Proof slot included" — is not exercised by anything in this diff. Every Machine clause (M1–M4) is pinned at `contendingBlock`, and the diff touches only `fleet/publish-fold-block.mjs`, `fleet/CONTRACT.md` and `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold_block.mjs`; the block→brief edge lives in `fleet/publish-fold.mjs:501` (`blocks.push(await buildContendingBlock(...))`) and `:531` (`open, contendingBlock: block`), which this patch does not touch and which stand unchanged at BASE. That edge is what makes a body the block carries a body the brief carries, and the task's Context asserts it rather than testing it. What would settle it: a leg in `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs` asserting the resolver prompt contains a frontier task's `**Proof:**` slot for a claims-v1 tag carrying its record — a file outside this task's FILES, so it is not this submission's to add.; fleet/publish-fold-block.mjs: the record's destination name is built from a hardcoded stem — `path.join(dir, 'plan' + GATE_VERDICTS_SUFFIX)` — rather than from `planFile`, the variable that actually decides the stem the compiler derives its sibling name from. The two are four lines apart today, so behaviour is correct and the exam passes; but if `planFile` is ever renamed, the record is silently written under a name the compiler does not look for and every claims-v1 frontier tag degrades back to a `no plan` line with no error anywhere — the exact failure this task exists to remove. Deriving the name from `planFile` makes the coupling unbreakable.

Advisory (no requirement gap): `EXAM_CHECK.run` invokes `ctx.exec(argv[0], argv.slice(1), { cwd: ctx.integ })` with no `timeoutMs` (fleet/publish-fold.mjs:218). The exams it runs are test files named by a *sibling run's* plan, fetched from that run's `ultra/plan/run-<M>` tag, so the fold now executes code it did not author with unbounded runtime, before the suite and while the branch already points at the candidate. A hanging exam wedges the fold with no diagnostic; `execSeam` already carries the `timeoutMs` seam added for exactly this (#436, fleet/run-main.mjs:177) and reports `timedOut` plus a stderr note, which would land in `exam-<attempt>-<n>.txt` and in the retry brief's tail. Passing a bound (e.g. `{ cwd: ctx.integ, timeoutMs: <n>s }`) changes neither the recorded `cmd`/`argv`/`cwd` the legs assert nor any `checks` shape, so it is compatible with the pinned exam. The task's M2 does not require it, and BASE's own `bash -lc` suite call is likewise unbounded, so this blocks nothing — it is recorded because the exam check widens what the fold will execute.; unverified: the exam evidence for this task is a single invocation — `node fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs fleet/tests/test_publish_fold_block.mjs` — which runs only the first path and passes the second as `process.argv[2]`; the combined output carries exactly one `ALL TESTS PASSED` line, and both sims end with that same line. So the Proof's second `Test:` path, `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold_block.mjs`, was almost certainly not executed: neither this task's two new `contendingTasks` regions in it (the four-commit frontier list `[['3','T1'],['7','A'],['7','C']]`, the untouched-path list, and the three-tag record list `[['11','1'],['13','T1'],['7','W']]` with its byte-for-byte `contendingBlock` re-pins) nor Task 3's whole region stands on executed evidence. I read every symbol those legs reach — `buildFixture`, `buildRecordFixture`, `compiledTaskWithRecord`, `CLAIMS_PLAN`, `CLAIMS_RECORD`, `PLAN_RUN13`, `TASK_W`, `heading`, `noPlanLine`, `taskEntry`, and `fx.run12` off `buildRecordFixture`'s return — and all are module-scope in the file at BASE, so the legs should resolve; but that is a reading, not a run. What would settle it: run the two sims as two commands (`node fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs && node fleet/tests/test_publish_fold_block.mjs`) and expect two `ALL TESTS PASSED` lines. The fix is to the TEST COMMAND, not to anything inside this task's FILES.; unverified: this task edits `fleet/CONTRACT.md`, and the global constraint names `tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py` as the lens for that file — but it is Task 1's Proof that carries `Run: python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py`, and Task 1 landed at BASE, before these two sentences changed. Task 2's Proof has only the two `grep -q` literals (green in RUN EVIDENCE), so no executed check covers the docs pin over the new text. The edits are additive inside two existing sentences and the pin reads literals rather than whole sentences (`tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py:54` onward), so the risk is low. What would settle it: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py` on this tree.; `fleet/CONTRACT.md`: the dispositions bullet is hand-wrapped to ~100 columns throughout, but the rewrite leaves one ~160-column line — `A \`hold=1\` run still folds — only its merge is skipped — and keeps \`left open: hold=1\`. Amendment 10 holds inside the fold: the only model it may`. The three lines this task added above it wrap correctly; only the seam line does not. Cosmetic, but this file is the plan's authority for literals and its wrap is uniform.; `fleet/publish-fold.mjs`: `EXAM_CHECK.run` calls `contendingTasks(...)` once per joined path, and `contendingTasks` builds a fresh `plans` Map per call — so for a candidate with P joined paths the frontier is walked P times, every `ultra/plan/run-<M>` tag is fetched P times, and `compile_plan.py` is spawned P times per plan, then all of it again on the retry pass. Leg (j) already pays this twice per pass for two paths. The exams themselves are deduped by `seen`; the plan compiles are not. A small memo around the per-attempt call — e.g. hoist a `Map` keyed by path outside the `for (const p of ctx.joined)` loop, or have `contendingTasks` accept a shared `plans` cache — removes P−1 subprocess compiles per pass without changing any recorded call the legs assert on (they filter on `node`/`bash -lc`, not on `python3 compile_plan.py`).; `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs`: the `// #754 Task 2` block re-declares `withIndex`, `word`, `parseCalls`, `suiteCalls`, `verbCalls`, `indexAt`, `parse`, `secondLine`, the `runIn` execFile wrapper and the `sentence` slicer as near-verbatim copies of the same helpers in the `// #751 Task 1` block (lines 1318–1335 and 1620–1638 at BASE). The duplication is largely forced by the plan's region discipline — Task 1's helpers are block-scoped, and hoisting them would edit Task 1's region, which the global constraint on BASE assertions makes costly — so this is a note rather than a demand. If the two regions are ever consolidated, these ten helpers are the seam: lift them to module scope beside `norm` and `git` and delete both copies.
